newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee seen sideways, lacking direction.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee seen sideways, lacking direction.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
Coffee is likely to trade sideways, staying in a range between $1,700 and $2,000 in the near term, analysts said.
Traders expected little movement on opening.
"I haven't got much of a view on direction as there isn't really a direction," Adrian Haylor, analyst at Sucden, said.
"It should hold support and go sideways." He put initial support at $1,775, with further support at $1,695.

There was little fundamental news to inspire the market. A senior official at Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said on Friday he saw the country's 1997/98 coffee crop coming in at about 12 million 60-kg bags.
Brazil's coffee regions should see warm weather over the coming five days, with no damaging cold in sight, local meteorologists Somar said on Sunday.
The forecast will come as welcome news to producers who have seen early hopes of a good quality harvest dashed by the recent rains which have disrupted the harvest and hit quality.
New York coffee futures ended mixed in thin choppy trade on Friday as light speculative selling was offset by trade buying toward the lows, dealers said.
LIFFE robusta coffee futures reversed direction to end slightly lower on Friday due to pre-weekend profit taking.
